title: verdict
description: One Type-B verdict (Implementation Decisions 11): what one verifier session answered about one subject. pass, findings and question_limit are the session's; session_id and model are filled in by code from the envelope, because a session knows neither.

pass.description: true when the subject answers the question; false carries at least one finding

findings.description: what is wrong, each at the path and locator it was read at; empty on a pass

text.description: what is wrong, in one or two sentences

locator.description: the path, with the line or the heading in it, the finding was read at

severity.description: blocker fails the subject on its own; major and minor are worth fixing

question_limit.description: the one question this verdict answers, restated in your own words; a verdict that answers a wider question is out of its scope

code_rule.description: only when the question lists a ticket's parameter reasons or its not_methods (the rule from code to Methods, ticket 107): your judgment of each; one that does not hold fails the verdict and is also a finding

holds.description: true when the reason justifies the value to a reader of Methods
true when it is indeed not a method the paper's Methods should describe

inherited.description: only when the question lists a ticket's verdicts on inherited claims (ticket 97): your check of each, by the claim's P id; one that does not hold fails the verdict and is also a finding

holds.description: true when the finding's evidence bears out the verdict it gives on the inherited claim, by the route it names

objective_judgments.description: only when the question lists objective proposals to judge (decision 17): your judgment of each, by its number in the list; a proposal not upheld is no finding and does not fail the verdict

upheld.description: true when the work's evidence bears the change out

answer.description: for an answer proposal you uphold: the objective's answer as you write it, every claim sentence ending with its {res:...} or {ref:...} tag; code checks its numbers and its locators

objective_proposals.description: changes to the objectives you propose yourself from what you read (decision 17), in the result's shape; they go on to be approved without a further judgment

kind.description: add a question, answer an open objective, park one for later, drop one, reframe one as a successor question, or reopen one that is parked, answered, or dropped

objective.description: the objective's id in OBJECTIVES.md (O2); for add, the new question's text

successor.description: for reframe only: the question that replaces the objective, in one sentence

reason.description: why the objective should change, from what the work found

evidence.description: locators in the linter's res: and ref: forms that bear the reason out

oneOf.description: for add and reframe: the position memo's row for the new question

session_id.description: written by the harness from the session's envelope; leave it out

model.description: written by the harness from the session's envelope; leave it out

proposals.description: tickets the verifier or the critic propose, taken through admission (ticket 37) exactly as a worker's result's
